justifications.durability: the drain-half guard fires: mutating run_paths_stage to ignore --flush (triage_only=options.flush -> triage_only=False) fails test_flush_runs_only_draining_workers at tests/cli/test_discover_paths_stage.py:82 with 'assert 1 == 0', where the unmutated head gate passes it (my own negative-control.log, EXIT=1); the reviewed run's declared negative control records the same test red at EXIT=1, and the mutual-exclusion and manifest-scope guards are additionally pinned by test_flush_refuses_add_roots and test_scan_only_and_flush_are_mutually_exclusive.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed head gate (12 passed, EXIT=0 at 404da8bd) I reproduced independently in a scratch checkout of 404da8bd (12 passed, EXIT=0), and I ran the regression surface the node's own arms omitted, tests/discovery/test_paths_pipeline.py, at both reviewed revisions (3 passed EXIT=0 each, module resolved from each scratch tree). The shortfall is on the record, not the code: the reviewed manifest declares no baseline_suite/after_suite, its gate2.log/gate3.log name revision e4ff44bb while the tree was modified (10/12 and 12/12 under a base revision header), and none of the node's arms include test_paths_pipeline.py, so a reader cannot derive added failures from the node's own logs.
justifications.fit: the added symbols PathsStageOptions, run_paths_stage and _focus_roots are named by what they do with no plan label or section number, and paths.py follows the sibling discover folds' stage-plus-thin-wrapper idiom; the only stale spelling in source is the pre-existing usage examples in the docstring and the 'discover paths' message strings, which the later retire-domain-subcommands node owns.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all four done-when behaviours and the settled option spellings are present and named by mechanism: run_paths_stage routes --scan-only to the seeding half, --flush to the draining half (paths.py:95 triage_only=options.flush), --topic to the engine focus, --limit to path_limit, and --focus items or a manifest file through _focus_roots; the default gate is get_path_scan_threshold() rather than the 0.9 default, which the plan required for this fold. The shortfall is that the plan says the engine-building body is 'kept whole, so no engine changes', and this fold did change _run_iterative_discovery (worker counts, seeding gate, check_ssh, and three new worker-count kwargs to run_parallel_discovery); those edits are what make the halves real, so they are justified, but they are a deviation from the stated extraction shape, and the plan's per-fold evidence fragment was not produced.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses _run_iterative_discovery, run_parallel_discovery, seed_facility_roots and get_path_scan_threshold unchanged and forks no engine; the three new worker-count kwargs it passes (num_expand_workers/num_enrich_workers/num_score_workers) already exist on run_parallel_discovery (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:2634-2637), so no engine parameter was invented; a search of imas_codex/cli found no earlier owner of a paths stage and no shared items-or-manifest reader that _focus_roots duplicates.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat e4ff44bba7688c71535eeacdd8086c8dc6d5b51a..404da8bd59fa9fb7217764b2dd8823c626ee09bc touches only imas_codex/cli/discover/paths.py and tests/cli/test_discover_paths_stage.py, both inside the declared write paths, with no edit to imas_codex/cli/discover/__init__.py, no dependency change and no unrelated file; the declared fragment and figures dir were not produced, which is an evidence shortfall rather than scope creep.
